sources.citation: Z'graggen, J. A. 1980. A comparative word list of the Rai Coast languages, Madang Province, Papua New Guinea. Pacific Linguistics D-30. Canberra: ANU. xvi+196 pp. doi:10.15144/PL-D30 (Pulabu = language B10)
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing. Intro sec. 7 (p. vii): transcription 'rendered in a semiphonemic form'; p. viii fluctuation table has a Pulabu heading with only dashes; no mention of stress/accent/tone anywhere (note 3 p. 172 concerns Dumpu-Watiwa being tonal). B10 Pulabu forms carry aspiration, length and trill marks but no stress marks (visual check printed p. 3).

sources.citation: Z'graggen, J. A. 1975a. The Madang-Adelbert Range Sub-Phylum. In S. A. Wurm (ed.), New Guinea area languages and language study 1 (Pacific Linguistics C-38), 569-612. Canberra: ANU.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing. Sec. 2.8.2.2.1.1.2: Kabenau Family = Arawum, Kolom, Suroi, Lemio, Pulabu; 'Arawum and Pulabu are new members. Zoller's (1891) word list of Kadda belongs to the Pulabu language.' Population B10 Pulabu 116; Table I structural features (Pulabu the Rai Coast exception for object-marker suffixing). No prosody.

sources.citation: Z'graggen, J. A. 1971. Classificatory and typological studies in languages of the Madang District. Pacific Linguistics C-19. Canberra: ANU. doi:10.15144/PL-C19
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Does not cover Pulabu: ch. 2.4 lists Pulabu (68) among Bogadjim Census Division villages 'linguistically still unknown'. Its survey-wide sentence (p. 6) 'The marking of stress has been omitted, since the stress patterning has not been well established yet' therefore does not apply to Pulabu data.

sources.citation: Claassen, Oren R. & Kenneth A. McElhanon. 1970. Languages of the Finisterre Range - New Guinea. Papers in New Guinea Linguistics 11 (Pacific Linguistics A-23), 45-78. Canberra: ANU.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Pulabu not named (their Kabenau Family = Kolom, Suroi, Lemio, Gurumbu, Watiwa). Sec. 6.1: 'In Suroi stress is contrastive, but only on a limited number of words' (sister language); nothing on Pulabu.
